title: Prior and future winter warmth gave uncertain richness slope contrasts in four British moth samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether winter warmth before the flight season had a different link to moth richness than winter warmth after that season. We used 685 ECN trap-months from England and Scotland in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. Richness was set to the expected taxon count at 100 caught individuals. Models controlled trap by month, sample effort, current monthly weather, winter rain and time. Prior-minus-future winter slopes ranged from -0.55 to +0.98 taxa per C. All four intervals included zero after correction for four tests. The early English contrast was positive with an ordinary 95 percent interval, but did not repeat in the later period. Some early English checks were positive after correction. This result does not show that winter warmth has no effect. Few year clusters, coarse country weather, selected catches and unknown detection rates limit inference. This is a time-order check, not a causal climate effect. Pollution and daily extremes were not tested.

display.caption: Points show prior-minus-future winter warmth slopes for richness at 100 individuals. Thin dark bars show ordinary 95 percent year-cluster intervals. Wide pale bars show intervals corrected for four tests. All four corrected intervals include zero.
